name: Anidulafungin
executiveSummary: IV echinocandin. Adult candidemia: load **200 mg on day 1**, then **100 mg every 24 h**. Pediatrics: load **3 mg/kg**, maintenance **1.5 mg/kg every 24 h**. Infusion ≤1.1 mg/min.
indications:
## Indications

- Invasive candidiasis / candidemia in non-neutropenic patients (and institutional neutropenic regimens).
- Esophageal candidiasis (lower doses on some labels).
- Restricted / combination use in refractory IFI per transplant/heme protocols.

## Precautions

- No bolus. Rate **<1.1 mg/min** (100 mg ≈ 90 min; 200 mg load ≈ 180 min).
- Infusion-related reactions — slow the rate.
- Little renal adjustment; hepatic metabolism without major CYP.

> No mucorales coverage; limited in urine.

adulto.dose: Candidemia / invasive: load **200 mg IV day 1**, maintenance **100 mg every 24 h**. Esophageal (label): often load **100 mg**, then **50 mg/day**.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute 30 mL SW; dilute in NS/D5W; infuse ≤1.1 mg/min.
adulto.notes: Reconstituted: dilute promptly (~1 h refrigerated in vial).

pediatrico.dose: Load **3 mg/kg** (max **200 mg**), then **1.5 mg/kg every 24 h** (max **100 mg**).
pediatrico.notes: Follow age band authorized on local label.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: ~1 h refrigerated; dilute immediately.
- Diluted: up to ~48 h room temp (label).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypokalemia, diarrhea, ↑ ALT/AST/ALP/bilirubin, infusion reactions (rash, pruritus, dyspnea, hypotension).
